message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze this situation carefully.

The position: Rhea Lend (ex-Burrow) on NEAR, contract.main.burrow.near, supplies native USDC (~$1,000), no debt.

Timeline:
- O01 (Apr 15, 22:48): Suspicious account deletions, but no interaction with burrow contract. Probably precursor noise.
- O02-O12: Progressive drain of USDC/USDT/wNEAR/ZEC held balances vs ledger-available. Classic exploit pattern: fake token contracts, fresh Ref pools created minutes earlier, margin positions opened via margin_execute_with_pyth using fake pools to mislead oracle — attacker extracts real assets (USDC, USDT, wNEAR, ZEC) from the lending contract.
- O07-O08: Attacker creates fake pools and opens margin positions.
- O13-O15: Guardian disables asset capacities for all assets — effectively pausing deposits/withdrawals/borrowing on the lending contract. This means withdrawals are paused for USDC (native USDC disabled at 09:54:46).
- O16: Burrow DAO proposals to unregister margin dexes (ref-exchange, ref-dcl) — mitigation.
- O17 (14:55): CertiK security alert: Rhea Finance exploited, ~$7.6M extracted.
- O18 (15:33): Official-ish X post confirming exploit, withdrawals paused.
- O19 (16:20): v2.ref-finance.near paused by guardian. Attacker account sends NEAR transfer to burrow contract.

Current time: 2026-04-16T16:20:53Z.

Key question: what action? The position is $1,000 USDC supplied on Rhea Lend. The protocol has been exploited (~$7.6M extracted). Withdrawals are paused — guardian disabled all asset capacities including native USDC (can_withdraw=false). The DEX is paused too.

So the user cannot withdraw right now — the keeper "cannot move funds, only propose an action; the corridor limits enforce safety." The action options: hold, reduce_light, reduce_to_target, exit, relever.

Given an active exploit with withdrawals paused, the risk is critical. But what action? Exit would be the desired action but withdrawals are paused — can_withdraw=false for USDC. The prompt says "you cannot move funds, only propose an action; the corridor limits enforce safety." So we propose exit; the corridor limits will enforce whether it can execute. Hmm, but if withdrawals are paused, proposing exit is still the right intent — the keeper should signal desire to exit as soon as possible. Alternatively, hold because nothing can be done?

Let me think about the design intent. The system prompt says: "Staying put during a real incident can leave funds stuck or lost even when prices look normal (exploits, oracle faults, bad collateral, liquidity runs, pauses and freezes)." This is exactly that scenario. The action should be exit — propose to unwind the whole position now. Even if paused, the corridor limits enforce safety; the keeper proposes. Actually, wait — if withdrawals are paused, an exit attempt would fail. But the risk framework likely wants "exit" as the signal of maximum defensiveness. Hmm.

Alternatively, some designs would say: since withdrawals are paused and funds are stuck, the action is "hold" because no action is executable. But the instruction says "you cannot move funds, only propose an action; the corridor limits enforce safety" — meaning we propose, and the enforcement layer decides feasibility. So proposing exit is correct: it expresses the intent to leave as soon as withdrawal reopens, and the corridor will block if not possible.

Risk level: critical. Active confirmed exploit on the exact venue and asset (USDC was among stolen assets; native USDC disabled). ~$7.6M extracted. Withdrawals paused. The user's $1,000 USDC is at risk of being stuck or lost (bad debt socialization possible).

Action: exit.

Reasons:
- Confirmed exploit on Rhea Finance (~$7.6M) via fake token pools misleading oracle; stolen assets include USDC — same asset as position.
- Onchain shows near-total drain of held USDC/USDT/wNEAR/ZEC vs ledger liabilities (held/ledger ~10% then lower), indicating the protocol owes far more than it holds.
- Guardian disabled all asset capacities including native USDC (withdrawals paused); DEX paused — funds currently stuck; exit intent should be registered for when withdrawals reopen.
- Attacker infrastructure (fresh implicit accounts, self-created Ref pools) interacted directly with contract.main.burrow.near.

Source ids: O07, O08, O09, O11, O14, O15, O17, O18, O19. Maybe also O05, O06, O10. Keep it focused: O08 (attack txs on the contract), O09/O11 (drain), O14 (USDC disabled), O17 (CertiK), O18 (confirmation), O19 (pause/attacker activity). I'll include a reasonable set.

Risk: critical. Action: exit.

One nuance: with withdrawals paused, exit can't execute now. But the framework says corridor limits enforce safety; proposing exit is the correct posture. Also note the attacker sent NEAR to the contract at 16:20 — ongoing activity. The position is supply-only USDC; USDC held is ~0.889M vs 9.81M ledger-available (~9% backing). Even if withdrawal reopens, there may be a run; getting out first matters. So exit.
